newsitem.title: Belgium: CLABECQ STILL FAVOURS WALLOON STEEL MERGER.
newsitem.headline: CLABECQ STILL FAVOURS WALLOON STEEL MERGER.

text.p: Belgian steel group Forges des Clabecq said on Thursday it saw closer links between steel firms in Belgium's francophone Walloon region as a way to ensure its survival and the preservation of jobs in the area.

"It is clear that we have a favourable attitude...to a rapprochment...as defended by (Walloon) Prime Minister Robert Collignon," Clabecq chief executive officer Libert Froidmont told the annual general meeting.
Clabecq is in the middle of a restructuring after a global economic deterioration, competition from low price imports, a weak dollar and steady stock levels hit results.
Fellow steel firms in the region include Usines Gustave Boel and bourse-listed Cockerill Sambre SA .
Froidmont noted the "abnormally" low prices had attracted buying and order books had risen consequently.

After having fallen by 1,000 to 1,200 francs a tonne, prices were now showing concrete signs of going up. In September prices rose by about 400 francs a tonne and in October increases of 250 to 300 francs a tonne were recorded.

Under the restructuring Clabecq plans to cut staff by 700 over two years. Before the end of 1996 some 400 are to go. At the end of September -- the first quarter of the 1996/97 bookyear -- Clabecq employed 1,889, down from 2,145 on January 31, 1996.
The company was currently studying ways of introducing additional cost-cutting.
At the end of the first quarter losses at Clabecq deepened.
Losses after financial charges and depreciations stood at 521.7 million francs. The company ended the 1995/96 year with a comparable loss of 780.7 million.

Shareholders equity was negative at the end of the first quarter to the tune of some 500 million francs, partly due to a delay in a planned capital increase by its majority shareholder SWS, the Walloon steel sector investment vehicle.
The 1.5 billion franc increase, decided on in June, is on hold pending European Union approval.
EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has expressed doubts about Clabecq's viability, noting there is still overcapacity in the steel sector.
